newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's peseta expected to hold steady after cut.
newsitem.headline: Spain's peseta expected to hold steady after cut.

text.p: The peseta shrugged aside a sharp 50 basis point reduction in Spain's money market rate on Thursday, but the cut should curb the currency's chances of rising through 84.00 per mark, analysts said.

The Bank of Spain slashed its repurchase rate to 6.75 percent from 7.25 percent, the sixth reduction this year, in recognition of the austere 1997 budget draft the government presented to parliament on Monday, analysts said.

With the cut, the central bank should be able to leave the currency market alone after reportedly intervening repeatedly in recent days to restrain the peseta's dogged efforts to press through the 84.00 level, analysts said.
At 1145 GMT, the peseta was at 84.19/20 per mark, slightly weaker than late Wednesday's 84.10/12.
"One of the things that dictated the size of the move as well has been the peseta, which I think the authorities would like to see a bit lower" Phylis Reed, economist at BZW in London told RFTV.
Forex dealers were little surprised by the peseta's strength on the European crosses as the interest rate cut had been widely expected and had largely been discounted in prices.

"There isn't anything else today behind the peseta's strength other than that the market had already discounted the cut and other international factors such as a weaker mark," a chief dealer in a Spanish institution said.
Although the peseta had already absorbed much of the recent good news, analysts said they expected it to remain strong short-term as the mark falters, although it was unlikely to strengthen further.
"All the good news -- from the official rate cut to the Euro convergency -- has been already factored in," said Almudena Isasi, economist at Analistas Financieros Internationales.
"But right now we see a weaker mark against the U.S. dollar and versus the Italian lira too...I think the risk that the peseta will go beneath 84 is very low," Isasi said.
Medium-term the peseta might have the strength to ease past 84.00 to, say, 83.80, should the U.S. currency remain strong and push down the German mark.
The peseta hit a recent peak of 84.02 on September 23, when the rumours of central bank intervention started.
However if the dollar corrects its upward trend -- considered a more likely scenario -- analysts see the peseta weakening and could move towards 84.70 per mark.
Chartists put support for the peseta at 84.20, than 84.50 and 84.70.
